title: How a claw hammer pulls out nails
examples: How does a hammer pull out a nail?
Why is it easy to pull a nail with a claw hammer?
Where is the pivot on a claw hammer?

explain.say: To pull a nail, you hook the hammer's split claw under the nail head and pull the handle back. The curved head rocks on the wood, which acts as the pivot, or fulcrum.

draw.text: How a claw hammer pulls out nails

explain.say: Your hand pulls at the end of the long handle, far from the pivot, making a big turning effect.
The nail sits in the claw very close to the pivot, so the claw pulls on it with many times your force, enough to beat the friction holding it in the wood.
That makes the claw hammer a first-class lever: effort and load on opposite sides of the pivot. A longer handle, or a block of wood under the head as the nail rises, keeps the advantage high.

faq.q: Where is the pivot on a claw hammer?
faq.a: When pulling a nail, the curved back of the hammer head presses on the wood and acts as the pivot. The handle and the claw are on opposite sides of it.
asks: What is the fulcrum of a claw hammer?

faq.q: How does a hammer pull out a nail?
faq.a: The hammer becomes a lever. A pull at the end of the long handle makes a large turning effect, and the claw, close to the pivot, pulls on the nail with a much bigger force.
asks: Why is it easy to pull a nail with a claw hammer?

faq.q: What holds a nail in the wood?
faq.a: Friction. When a nail is driven in, the wood fibres are pushed aside and press tightly on it. Pulling it out means overcoming that grip.
asks: Why are nails hard to pull out?

faq.q: Why put a block under the hammer head?
faq.a: As the nail rises, the pivot gets close to your hand and the claw tilts. A block raises the pivot so the claw stays close and you keep the force advantage.
asks: Why does a nail get harder to pull near the end?

faq.q: What kind of lever is a claw hammer?
faq.a: Used to pull nails, it is a first-class lever, with the pivot between your effort and the load, like a seesaw or a crowbar.
asks: Is a hammer a first class lever?

facts: A claw hammer pulling a nail is a first-class lever, like a crowbar.
The longer the handle compared with the claw's distance from the pivot, the bigger the force on the nail.

quiz.say: The handle grip is 30 cm from the pivot and the nail 3 cm. You pull with 50 newtons. Roughly what force pulls the nail?
quiz.show: The handle grip is 30 cm from the pivot and the nail 3 cm. You pull with 50 newtons. Roughly what force pulls the nail?
quiz.why: 30 divided by 3 is 10, and 10 times 50 newtons is 500 newtons.

wrong.1: That multiplies by 3, but the distance ratio is 10.
wrong.2: The lever multiplies your force; the nail gets more than you put in.
